The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today said that amid a world weighed down by conflicts and contradictions, the successful BRICS summit held in New Delhi stands out as truly remarkable.Addressing the Silver Jubilee Celebration of the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA) as an Institution of National Importance in the national capital, he praised the unanimously adopted New Delhi Declaration as a major achievement. He noted that ICWA will play a key role in the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047 because the organization has the legacy, institutional framework, and intellectual tradition.Speaking on the occasion, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that India is articulating with greater confidence its perspectives on global challenges, including those that concern the Global South. He said that the country’s interests have become increasingly global, its responsibilities have grown, and expectations of India have also risen correspondingly.Dr Jaishankar underlined that as a country’s global role is growing, the intellectual engagement with international affairs must keep pace. He also highlighted that a rising India must increasingly bring its own history, experience, interests, concepts, and even terminology to the way it approaches the world.The Indian Council of World Affairs was established in 1943 by a group of Indian intellectuals as a think tank. It was registered as a non-official, non-political and non-profit organisation under the Registration of Societies Act 1860. By an Act of Parliament in 2001, the Indian Council of World Affairs has been declared an institution of national importance. The Vice President of India is the ex-officio President of ICWA.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. US President Donald Trump has said Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop attacking each other’s energy targets, without giving a start date, duration or enforcement details. In a social media post, Trump said Ukraine had agreed not to hit Russian energy targets and Russia had agreed to do likewise. However, the post did not specify which facilities would be covered or whether either side had attached conditions.The Kremlin has welcomed Trump’s call for Ukraine to halt strikes on Russia’s fuel-producing facilities. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that countries with influence over Ukraine could encourage Kyiv to show greater flexibility, which he said would make a significant contribution to efforts to resolve the conflict. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready to halt strikes on Russian territory if its allies can secure a genuine Russian commitment not to attack Ukraine’s critical infrastructure.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar will be on a two-day official visit to Bhutan from today. During the visit, Dr Jaishankar will hold bilateral talks with the Foreign Minister of Bhutan Lyonpo D.N. Dhungyel. He will receive a royal audience with the King of Bhutan and call on the Prime Minister of Bhutan.The Ministry of External Affairs said the visit is in keeping with the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between India and Bhutan and to further strengthen the existing close ties of friendship and cooperation between the two countries.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Afghanistan by 7 wickets in the first T20 International at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi last night, taking a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.After India won the toss and chose to bowl first, Afghanistan struggled early and collapsed to 43 for 5. A strong 83-run partnership between Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi pushed Afghanistan’s final score to 156 for 8 in 20 overs. For India, Arshdeep Singh picked up 3 wickets for 19 runs.India chased down the target comfortably, reaching 157 for 3 in just 13.4 overs with 38 balls left. Opener Abhishek Sharma was named Player of the Match for a blistering 82 runs off 32 balls, sharing a massive 121-run stand with Ishan Kishan.The remaining two matches of the series will be played at the same venue on Tuesday and Thursday.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. The Ministry of External Affairs has said that several issues came up during the discussion between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Addressing media in New Delhi this evening, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that during the meeting, Prime Minister referred to India’s concerns and underlined that both sides should show sensitivity to each other’s core concerns. He added that the concerns should be be guided by the three mutuals which are mutual respect, mutual interest, and mutual sensitivity.In reply to a question on the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman,  Mr Jaiswal said that targeting commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable to India. He said, India also urges that free and safe navigation, as well as the flow of commerce through international waterways in the region, be restored at the earliest. He said, the attack on the vessel occurred off the coast of Oman involving a Panama-flagged vessel carrying 14 Indian national seafarers. He said, of them , 13 have been rescued and one Indian national, a seafarer who was on board the vessel, remains missing. Mr Jaiswal informed that search and rescue operations are continuing with the assistance of the Omani authorities, and Indian Embassy is in close contact with them.When asked about the reward of 70 lakh Pakistani rupees announced by Pakistan on Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar, the spokesperson said that such gimmicks and attempts at hoodwinking by Pakistan are not new as India has seen similar gimmicks in the past as well. Mr Jaiswal said that Pakistan must take concrete action rather than making  announcements that are of no consequence.Replying to another query, Mr Jaiswal said the energy cooperation between India and Russia is an important pillar of the bilateral partnership. He pointed out that both countries have been collaborating for a long time now on nuclear sector. He added that the Kudankulam project is a successful example of India-Russia collaboration in the energy field. He said India wants to take this energy cooperation with Russia forward. He also informed that both sides have been in conversation, and technical teams have been in discussions.The spokesperson said External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar held a meeting with the Saudi Foreign Minister on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. During the meeting, they discussed regional and international developments. Mr Jaiswal said that the issue of the Houthis was also discussed. There was recently an attack on Saudi Arabia, which India has condemned. He further stated that New Delhi is deeply concerned with the escalation in the situation in the Red Sea region. India has condemned the attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, including on civilian infrastructure and economic assets. Mr Jaiswal said such attacks undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb. He termed these actions as unacceptable, and hoped for the early restoration of peace and stability in the region. He added that India continues to receive energy supplies from that part of the world.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi declined 0.8 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 remained largely unchanged.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.2 per cent, while Germany’s DAX was trading on a flat note, when reports last came in.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today laid emphasis on India’s strong commitment to multi-polarity, which emanates from independent stance and belief in strategic autonomy. Delivering the valedictory address of Silver Jubilee Celebration of Indian Council of World Affairs in Delhi, Dr Jaishankar expressed confidence that India is destined to rise in a turbulent world. He underscored the contemporary trends shaping India’s diplomacy and nation’s growing economy and capabilities in the last decade, and its implications for global engagement. The External Affairs Minister said Indian diplomacy will always have peace and development as its central agenda.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. Government has clarified that there will be no charges at all for person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions, irrespective of the amount transferred.Finance Ministry said that payments to merchants up to two thousand rupees, along with transactions covered under the zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for small merchants, will also remain free.The Ministry said that consequently, approximately 96 percent of all P2M transactions will remain unaffected. It said that MDR will apply only to specified merchant transactions above two thousand rupees.The Ministry said that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the government or the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It is distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers, to support the operation and continued expansion of the UPI ecosystem.NPCI has said that a revised UPI Merchant Discount Rate framework has been introduced on select merchant transactions, effective from 15th of next month, while keeping UPI free for consumers.Akashavni correspondent reports said that a dedicated fund for promoting use of UPI by small merchants will be set up with a contribution of 5 percent of total MDR collections.The Finance Ministry said that charges will apply only to person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions exceeding two thousand rupees. It said that UPI app providers are explicitly prohibited from levying platform fees or hidden charges.The Ministry said that banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges to customers for UPI payments.A nominal MDR of 0.4 percent will be levied on person-to-merchant transactions above 2,000 rupees, while for high-value transactions of 75 thousand rupees and above, MDR will be capped at three hundred rupees per transaction.The Ministry informed that small merchants receiving up to one lakh rupees per month via UPI QR codes under the Person to Person Merchant (P2PM) classification will continue to enjoy mandatory zero MDR for all transactions.Additionally, Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel sectors, agriculture inputs will pay a flat MDR of five rupees per transaction above two thousand rupees. It said there are no monthly quotas, volume limits, or tiered caps on free UPI transactions for individuals.The Ministry said that the MDR framework has been introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, following detailed deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee on the applicable rates, operational arrangements and consumer safeguards.The framework seeks to strengthen the long-term sustainability of UPI while keeping payments free for individuals and protecting small merchants.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Afghanistan by seven wickets in the second T20 International at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi last night, to take an unassailable 2-nil lead in the three-match series.Chasing a target of 160 runs, India comfortably reached 163 for 3 in 14.5 overs. Sanju Samson top-scored with a blistering 57 off 22 balls, while Abhishek Sharma contributed 39 runs off 19 balls. Ishan Kishan remained unbeaten on 38 off 23 balls to guide India home.Earlier, put into bat, Afghanistan posted 159 for 8 in their stipulated 20 overs. Captain Ibrahim Zadran was their top scorer, making 37 runs off 33 balls. For India, Nitish Kumar Reddy claimed three wickets, while Arshdeep Singh took two wickets.Reddy was adjudged Player of the Match. India had won the toss and elected to field. The third and final match of the series will be played at the same venue in Delhi tomorrow.

. Delhi Government has announced to double the fixed monthly incentive for ASHA workers from three thousand rupees to six thousand rupees.This decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta in New Delhi yesterday. She said that the increase in the monthly incentive was an important step towards recognising ASHA workers’ contribution and ensuring their financial security.Ms Gupta said that it will boost their enthusiasm for their work and help them continue their services. There are six thousand 725 ASHA workers currently working in Delhi. Generally, each ASHA worker is associated with around two thousand people or 400 families.Meanwhile, Dellhi Government has also decided to built hostels for 10,000 students studying in colleges and universities across the national capital. Delhi Chief Minister said that construction of hostels is already under way in some Delhi government universities and institutions.She said that the scope of the initiative will now be expanded in view of the growing need. Ms Gupta said that the government will also conduct a survey of colleges that have sufficient space for hostel construction. She said that the process of constructing hostels will be expedited after suitable locations are identified.
. In the forex market, the rupee depreciated by 41 paise to close at 95 rupees and 96 paise against the US dollar.

. The Country’s overall workforce participation rate (WPR) for age 15 years and above increased to 52.8 per cent in August, the highest level recorded since March, 2026. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, rural WPR increased by 1.3 per cent to 55.8 per cent, whereas the urban WPR declined half a per cent to stood at 47 per cent in August.The country’s unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above declined marginally to five per cent in August, compared with 5.1 per cent in July this year. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, the rural unemployment rate eased to 4.1 per cent in August, which is the lowest level since January this year. In contrast, the urban unemployment rate increased slightly to 6.8 per cent, marking a four-month high. Among females, the overall unemployment rate declined to 5.1 per cent, while the unemployment rate among males eased to 4.9 per cent in August.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for age 15 years and above increased moderately to 55.6 per cent in August.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today discussed opportunities to further deepen the India – Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) partnership. The Finance Minister met the President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Zou Jiayi, in New Delhi. In a social media post, the Finance Ministry said discussions were held on supporting India’s infrastructure and transport connectivity priorities, enhancing local-currency financing, increasing private-sector participation and the global presence of AIIB.

. In the Women’s T20 Asia Cup cricket final, India will face defending champions Sri Lanka in Dubai today. The match will begin at 8 PM Indian time. Both India and Sri Lanka have reached the final unbeaten.Seven-time champions India have reached the final topping Group A with three wins before defeating Bangladesh by 40 runs in the semi-final.Sri Lanka also remained unbeaten in the group stage, winning all three matches before overcoming Pakistan by four wickets in the semi-final. India are the most successful team in Women’s Asia Cup history with seven titles.

. In Bangladesh, the Election Commission (EC) has decided to hold Union Parishad (UP) elections across the country in seven phases, with the first phase likely to be held on November 12.Election Commissioner Brigadier General (Retd.) Abul Fazal Md. Sanaullah disclosed the information while speaking to journalists at the Election Building in the capital’s Agargaon.“Elections need to be held swiftly in around 4,272 UPs out of total 4,580 UPs as there is a legal obligation to hold elections within the 180-day period before the expiry of their terms,” he said.He added that the primary schedule for voting has been prepared considering the annual examinations of students and religious festivals.According to the announced schedule, voting in the first phase will be held on November 12 this year, the second phase on December 13 and the third phase on December 30.The preliminary dates for the fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh phases have been set for January 17, February 4, April 22 and May 27, respectively, in 2027.Besides, the Commission will hold dialogues with all registered political parties over three days on September 23, 24 and 25 to deliver a well-organised election like the national parliamentary election. Two representatives from each party will take part in the dialogues.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.7 per cent down at 1,50,902 rupees per 10 grams. Silver dipped marginally to 2,28,741 rupees per kilogram.

. India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament.India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match.India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title.President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours.Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has congratulated the Indian women’s cricket team via a social media post. Mr Birla lauded the team for remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament and securing victory in the Asia Cup for the 8th time. He added that the cricketers gave a splendid demonstration of their talent and determination in the tournament and this victory is a triumph of the strength, hard work, and dreams of the daughters of India. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that the accomplishment inspires the youth of the country, to dream big, work hard, and move forward with full determination to achieve their goals.

. The opening ceremony of the 22nd edition of the India-US joint military exercise ‘Yudh Abhyas’ was held at Auli in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand.The ceremony was conducted at the Auli Foreign Training Centre, with contingents of 600 personnel each from the two countries participating. The exercise is being conducted at Auli as well as the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan.Akashvani correspondent reports that the exercise aims to enhance the capabilities of both armies to conduct joint military operations in mountainous and semi-mountainous areas, with special emphasis on infantry-based operations.During the exercise, the two armies will exchange operational methods and strengthen joint planning and operations.The training will include the use of drones and autonomous systems for surveillance and reconnaissance.Modern weapon systems will also be demonstrated at the Mahajan Field Firing Range. Experts from both armies will exchange views on emerging technologies and developments related to multi-domain warfare.

. A US federal judge has temporarily blocked a new Trump administration rule imposing stricter limits on the duration of stay for foreign students and journalists in the United States. The ruling, delivered by a district judge in Massachusetts, is expected to provide relief to international students. The judge observed that implementation of the policy would probably cause catastrophic damage to the US economy and the higher education system.The Trump administration had finalised the rule in July this year. It proposed a four-year limit on visas for foreign students and exchange visitors, while journalists would have been permitted to stay for a maximum of 240 days. However, journalists from China would have been subject to a 90-day limit.Under the now-postponed policy, students and journalists could apply for extensions of their stay. However, approval would have remained at the discretion of officials of the Department of Homeland Security. The rule also provided no mechanism to appeal a decision denying an extension.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today emphasisied that self reliance in defence sector can be achieved through seamless collaboration among the Defence Forces, Research and Development institutions and the industry. He called for greater dialogue, co-development and co-production to accelerate technology adoption and strengthen India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Addressing the DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, ‘VIMARSH 2026’ in New Delhi, Mr Singh said that DRDO has demonstrated its capabilities in every field, from missiles to radars, combat aircraft to submarines, electronic warfare system to Artificial Intelligence.The Defence Minister said that the reforms witnessed in the defence sector over the past few years are unprecedented and several game-changing decisions have also been taken. These include the Positive Indigenisation List, the Make in India initiative, iDEX, ADITI and the decision to allocate 25 percent of the Defence Research and Development budget to the private sector. Mr Singh asserted that these measures have been taken to ensure that India does not remain dependent on imports in the defence sector, but moves towards self-reliance.Describing MSMEs as a backbone of the Indian economy, Mr Singh said that their contribution in components, sub-systems and essential services is significant in the defence sector. He added that  MSMEs will have to continuously focus on quality, delivery, innovation and global standards, as well as increase partnerships with large companies. The Defence Minister stressed that a new wave of defence startups is rising in India. He said that these startups are not only innovative but also agile and are disrupting the traditional defence manufacturing model. The Minister said that the opportunities in the defence sector have increased for them with funding, mentorship, and market access.Mr Singh underlined that the goal of Viksit Bharat is not merely to build an economically strong nation, but to also make it technologically self-reliant, socially inclusive, environmentally sustainable, and strategically secure. He emphasised that a nation that possesses its own technology holds the power to shape its own future, adding that self-reliance must become an integral part of the country’s character and attitude. During the event, nine licensing agreements for Transfer of Technology were handed over to 13 manufacturing partners to enable commercial production of state-of-the-art systems. DRDO also signed a contract with Quality Council of India for System for Advance Manufacturing Assessment and Rating version 2.0 to benchmark the manufacturing maturity of domestic defence enterprises.

. US-based analyst Michael Kugelman has described India’s hosting of the 18th BRICS Summit as a success, saying the substantive New Delhi Declaration reflects New Delhi’s ability to build consensus among countries with differing views.Michael Kugelman, a Senior Fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic Council, said the declaration reflects India’s growing convening power and the increasing appeal of the BRICS grouping. The two-day summit, held in New Delhi under India’s chairmanship, concluded on Sunday. BRICS comprises 11 major emerging economies, representing nearly half the world’s population and around 40 per cent of global GDP.The BRICS countries unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 on Saturday, with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping among the leaders attending. The declaration expressed serious concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort global trade and violate World Trade Organisation rules.It also stressed the need for cooperation on terrorism, conflict prevention and the peaceful resolution of disputes. Mr Kugelman said the declaration seeks to boost trade among BRICS nations and strengthen the grouping as an alternative to Western-led economic and financial institutions. He added that the push for greater intra-BRICS trade showed the bloc’s ability to deliver substantive measures for economies facing tariffs and sanctions linked to the Trump administration’s trade policies.

. India and Canada have begun the fourth round of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in New Delhi, as both sides seek to boost bilateral trade to 50 billion US dollars by 2030. The five-day talks, which began yesterday, will continue until September 18 and cover key areas including trade in goods and services, rules of origin, and technical trade barriers, among others.Bilateral trade between both the countries declined 8.22 percent to 7.95 billion US dollars in 2025-26 from 8.66 billion US dollars in 2024-25. India’s major exports to Canada include pharmaceuticals, iron and steel, seafood, cotton garments, electronics and chemicals, while key imports include pulses, pearls and semi-precious stones, coal, fertilisers, paper and crude oil. India’s main services sector exports to Canada include telecommunications, computer and information services, and other business services. Canada is also home to more than 425,000 Indian students and a large Indian-origin community. The third round of CEPA negotiations was held in Ottawa in July.

. India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI) based inflation rose marginally to 9.92 per cent in August, from 9.78 per cent in July, on an annual basis. According to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the annual inflation last month was driven by higher prices of mineral oils, food articles, food products, basic metals, non-food articles, chemicals and chemical products. The wholesale price inflation remained above the nine percent mark for the fourth consecutive month.Among the major categories in WPI, year over year inflation in the Fuel and Power group surged to 22.9 per cent last month, from 20 per cent in July. Inflation in Manufactured Products rose slightly to almost 8.4 per cent, from 8.3 per cent. Meanwhile, inflation in Primary Articles decreased to around 7.8 per cent in August, from 8.5 per cent in July. The WPI Food Index, which comprises food articles and food products, rose to 7.05 per cent in August, from 6.65 per cent in the previous month. The Output Producer Price Index increased by 9.81 per cent year-on-year in August.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative territory today. The Sensex plunged 778 points or one per cent to close at 74,004. The Nifty shed 280 points or 1.2 per cent to settle at 23,119.The broader market also witnessed a sharp decline, with the Nifty Midcap 100 index falling 2.1 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 index losing 2.4 per cent.

. In tennis, India’s SD Prajwal Dev, partnering France’s Constantin Bittoun Kouzmine, has won his second ATP Challenger doubles title at the Sport Festival Challenger in Phan Thiet, Vietnam.The top-seeded Indo-French duo defeated Japan’s Yamato Sueoka and Naoki Tajima 6-1, 7-6 in the final yesterday. This is Dev’s second ATP Challenger Tour doubles title. His maiden title came in 2023 at the President’s Cup in Kazakhstan, where he partnered fellow Indian Niki Kaliyanda Poonacha.The Challenger 50 event, played on hard courts, began on the 7th of this month and concludes today.

. Chief Ministers of Six States today signed the Kishau Multipurpose Dam Project agreement for the rejuvenation of the Yamuna River. These States are Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi. The agreement was signed in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi.Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah expressed confidence that once the project is completed, this event will become an important chapter in history. He said that the Central government has declared the Kishau Project a National Project. Mr Shah said, the Central Government will bear approximately 90 per cent of its financial burden, while the remaining 10 per cent will be borne by the participating states.The Minister said that ever since Rekha Gupta became the Chief Minister of Delhi, continuous work has been underway  to clean the Yamuna. He said that since Narendra Modi became Prime Minister, this is the tenth water related dispute, which is now set to be resolved. He said that first, in August 2018, the dispute over the Lakhwar Multipurpose Project was resolved. In the same month, the dispute over the Shahpur Kandi Dam Project was settled. In 2021, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh reached an agreement on the Ken-Betwa Link Project, benefiting the water-stressed region of Bundelkhand. The dispute over the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Narmada Project was resolved in July 2026.Union Minister for Jal Shakti C.R. Patil, Union Home Secretary, Union Secretary for Water Resources, and the Chief Secretaries of the concerned states were also present on this occasion.

. Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse said progress in sports is an important aspect of nation-building as India works towards its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.The Union Minister, who arrived in Mizoram on a three-day visit visited the Sports Authority of India centre at Mission Veng. There, she met Mizoram Sports Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar, officials of the Sports Department and representatives of various sports organisations, who apprised her of their needs and concerns.Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, Khadse said the government is making every effort to promote sports as it is an important part of nation-building under the ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ initiative. She said the government has launched Yuva Connect to enable sports to go hand in hand with education, with various programmes aimed at promoting sports being conducted in educational institutions.The Union Minister said Mizoram is doing well in various sports disciplines and praised the state’s efforts to identify and nurture young talent. She said she would make every effort to promote development across different sports disciplines.Khadse said young people are the vision of the nation and that the government gives them priority. She said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been taking steps to promote sports in India since 2014, with various developments taking place under the Khelo India programme.She said efforts are being made through various initiatives to produce more successful athletes, including identifying talented children in cities as well as remote areas, and that many have already benefited from such programmes. She said women’s sporting talent is also being promoted, but much more remains to be done. Stressing the importance of a systematic approach to sports, she said the government is making every effort to provide athletes with greater strength and support, including through proper nutrition, and to build the infrastructure needed for the overall development of sports.

. Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav underlined India’s commitment to embedding circular economy principles into its sustainable development framework.The Minister stressed that India has modernized it’s deep rooted ancient cultural practices of reuse, repair, and conservation values into contemporary policies under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Addressing the inaugural session of the 10th edition of World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026, at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar today, the Minister emphasised initiatives such as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations and Mission life as crucial steps in its circularity journey.Highlighting global collaborations like the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, India-EU joint framework, and Mission LiFE, the Minister stated that circularity must begin at home. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel inaugurated the forum which is being held for the first time in India.Addressing the Forum, the Chief Minister stressed that growth, ecology, prosperity, and sustainability must go hand in hand, framing circular economy principles as the core of India’s sustainable trajectory. Over 2,000 stakeholders from more than 65 countries are taking part in the forum which is being held under the theme ‘Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity,’. As of August 2026, over 83,000 producers and 4,802 recyclers are registered under EPR, processing nearly 482.24 lakh metric tonnes of waste.The global event is jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Central Pollution Control Board, Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, and the Government of Gujarat. Over the two days, the forum will host 4 plenary sessions and 16 thematic sessions covering key areas such as the application of AI, green energy, sustainable finance, governance, and the start-up ecosystem. This will be followed by 80 accelerator sessions hosted globally on September 17th and 18th. Additionally, an international expo featuring over 125 exhibitors will showcase innovative, practical solutions for circular business models.Speaking at the inaugural session, Ambassador of Finland to India, Mikko Kivikoski, said that circular economy is not just an environmental agenda which is limited to West management. He stressed that emerging economies like India has a pivotal role in strengthening the circular economy framework.

. Uttar Pradesh cabinet has approved the transfer of free land to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for the establishment of a Regional Centre of the National Security Guard (NSG) in Ayodhya.The decision was taken in a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath yesterday. The approval has been given to the proposal to transfer 26 hectares (or 65 acres) of barren land in Milkipur tehsil of Ayodhya to the MHA.Giving details about the decisions of the cabinet, Finance and Parliamentary Affairs Minister of State, Suresh Khanna, said that after the construction of the Ram Temple and its consecration ceremony, Ayodhya has emerged at the national and international level as a major cultural, religious and strategic centre.A large number of devotees, distinguished guests and tourists from the country and abroad are continuously visiting there. In such a situation, the security sensitivity of the area has also increased considerably.Keeping this in view, the minister said, permanent deployment of an NSG in Ayodhya through this regional centre has become necessary.The NSG centre is being set up to strengthen the security arrangements of Ram Temple and with a purpose of helping in dealing with any potential security challenge in Ayodhya, further strengthening the rapid response capability in any emergency situation.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. Global crude oil prices rose today on fears of supply disruptions after Saudi Arabia closed its East-West pipeline, with the duration of the closure remaining uncertain.Brent crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 106 US dollars and 10 cents per barrel in intra-day trade at a time of writing this report. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude was trading over one per cent higher at 102 US dollars and 47 cents per barrel.

. India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency is broadening historically strong oil-related ties with the Gulf into a wider partnership spanning investment, technology, food security, clean energy and regional stability, a report has said.The report published in a daily published from UAE said energy ties remain the foundation of the relationship at the 18th BRICS Summit, but cooperation is expanding into new strategic areas. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE this year, both the countries deepened collaboration on crude oil, LNG and LPG, and agreed to increase UAE participation in India’s strategic petroleum reserves and explored strategic gas reserves.Another area of co-operation is food-security which can link Gulf demand with India’s agricultural and food-processing capabilities. Investment in storage, logistics and reliable supply chains can be explored, the report noted. Highlighting the timing of the event, the report said that regional tensions have renewed attention on energy security, maritime trade and safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while Gulf states diversify their economies, invest in advanced technology and strengthen commercial links with Asia.The Gulf is represented in the expanded BRICS through Saudi Arabia and the UAE, providing the bloc greater weight in the global energy and finance landscape. India-Gulf ties grew stronger in February this year, when the country signed terms of reference with GCC and formally launched negotiations for a comprehensive free trade agreement, covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. In Para Badminton, Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat secured gold medal in the men’s singles SL3 category and teamed up with Sukant Kadam to win silver in the men’s doubles SL3-SU5 at the Japan International today. The six-time world champion, Bhagat produced a dominant performance in the singles final, defeating fellow Indian, Umesh Kumar 21-16, 21-8 to clinch the top honour. Bhagat then partnered Kadam in the men’s doubles SL3-SU5 category final, where the Indian pair went down 5-21, 15-21 to Indonesia’s Hikmat Ramdani and Fredy Setiawan, settling for silver. The tournament was particularly special for Kadam, who took his career medal tally to 100 over 12 years of competitive badminton.

. The conflict in West Asia is putting growing pressure on Saudi Arabia and key regional shipping routes, with fresh alerts, attacks and military exchanges reported.In Saudi Arabia, Civil Defence issued very brief emergency alerts in Makkah, Jeddah and Taif today, but the warnings were lifted within just a few minutes. Earlier, alerts had been issued and lifted in six cities, including Yanbu, Saudi Arabia’s main Red Sea oil port. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has said that 13 civilians were injured and seven homes and two vehicles were damaged in Monday’s Houthi attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif. The coalition said it will respond firmly and take necessary measures to protect the Kingdom.The humanitarian situation in Yemen is also worsening. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, has warned that rapidly escalating hostilities along Yemen’s western coast have displaced more than 100,000 people inside the country and forced thousands more to seek safety across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in Djibouti.In the Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO reported that a vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. Meanwhile, commercial vessel traffic through the Hormuz fell to just four commodity vessels on Monday, from ten the previous day, as per data available on Kpler – a platform tracking maritime flow and shipping data.Overall, the conflict is now putting simultaneous pressure on Saudi Arabia, the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, while diplomatic efforts between Iran and the Gulf states remain stalled after postponement of a meeting earlier scheduled on Monday.

. Top-ranked India’s Dhiraj Bommadevara scripted history by becoming the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the World Cup Final, edging Japan’s Nakanishi Junya in a thrilling shoot-off at Saltillo in Mexico.The 25-year-old World Number 10 Army man produced a dominant run, powering through the quarterfinals and semifinals before overcoming world No. 20 Nakanishi 6-5 in a hard-fought five-setter. After a 5-5 tie, Dhiraj prevailed 10-9 in the shoot-off. He also ended a 16-year wait for an Indian male recurve archer to win a medal in this prestigious event. Jayanta Talukdar was the last male recurve archer to win a medal – a bronze in Edinburgh 2010.Dola Banerjee remains the only other Indian to have won World Cup Final gold, claiming the women’s individual title in the 2007 edition in Dubai.

. Compelling a rape survivor to continue with a pregnancy resulting from the crime and fastening the responsibility of motherhood on her against her will would amount to a serious impairment of her right to live with dignity, the Delhi High Court has held. The court made the observations while allowing a plea on behalf of a 15-year-old rape survivor seeking the termination of her pregnancy, which had exceeded 30 weeks of gestation.Under Section 3 of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, termination of pregnancy beyond 20 weeks and up to 24 weeks is permissible in respect of specified categories of women, subject to the statutory requirements.Terming it an unfortunate and distressing case, Justice Madhu Jain said the fact that the pregnancy had crossed the statutory limit, by itself, could not be viewed in isolation. It said that a woman’s right in relation to her body necessarily included the right to decide whether or not she wished to become a mother.

. New Zealand’s Parliament has passed legislation to implement its free trade agreement with India, paving the way for significant reductions in tariffs and expanded trade between the two countries.The legislation was approved by a vote of 93-29, with support from the opposition Labour Party. New Zealand Trade Minister Todd McClay said the agreement would deliver “immediate and substantial” benefits for exporters. He said the high-quality trade deal is expected to enter into force later this year.Under the agreement, tariffs on about 95 percent of New Zealand’s exports to India will be eliminated or significantly reduced. More than half of the products covered by the deal will become duty-free from the day the agreement enters into force.All Indian goods will receive duty-free access to the New Zealand market. Wellington has also agreed to invest 20 billion US dollars in ​India over ​the next ⁠15 years.The two countries originally signed the trade agreement in April. Two-way trade between New Zealand and India totalled 2.29 billion US dollars in the year to June 2026, with India ranking as New Zealand’s ninth-largest market for goods and services exports.The agreement will take effect once both New Zealand and India complete their domestic ratification processes.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. World Ozone Day is being observed across the globe today. The day is dedicated to raising awareness about the crucial role of the ozone layer in safeguarding life on Earth.The theme for 2026 is “Global Action for a Cooler Planet.”  The theme highlights the achievements of international cooperation in protecting the ozone layer. It also connects ozone protection with climate-change action.The theme emphasises collective responsibility and sustained global action. It promotes the use of environmentally friendly technologies and safer alternatives. 2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol.The Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016. Often described as “Earth’s umbrella, the ozone layer acts as a protective shield, blocking harmful UV radiation from the sun. This natural barrier significantly reduces the risk of skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to ecosystems.Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Kirti Vradhan Singh said that the ozone layer is the shield against harmful UV rays.In a social media post, the Minister highlighted that the day reminds that protecting the ozone layer starts at home. He said that simple measures, like maintaining ACs at 24 degree Celsius and choosing efficient appliances, reduce emissions for a healthier Earth.Mr Singh said preserving the ozone layer safeguards human health, biodiversity and climate stability. He also called on the citizens to embrace sustainable practices for a safer future.

. Maharashtra Cabinet has approved soft loans of around 750 crore rupees for cooperative sugar mills to clear pending Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) dues to sugarcane farmers for 2025-26 crushing season and support operations for the 2026-27 season.The decision to approve soft loans of around 750 crore rupees for cooperative sugar mills was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis yesterday. The Chief Minister said the state government will bear the interest on these loans.Mr Fadnavis said the move will enable cooperative sugar mills to commence operations and procure sugarcane for the current crushing season, benefiting both mills and farmers. Speaking to reporters after the meeting,Mr Fadnavis said that Maharashtra has achieved nearly 99.5 per cent payment of FRP to sugarcane farmers and is now first in the country in terms of FRP clearance.

. Saudi Arabia has said that its air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone near Makkah last evening. The spokesperson for the ‘Coalition Forces to Support Legitimacy in Yemen’, Major General Turki Al-Maliki, described the incident as the second attempted Houthi attack on Makkah, referring to an earlier ballistic missile incident in 2017.He also warned that the Saudi-led coalition would take necessary measures against further attacks. Meanwhile, the Houthis have denied targeting Makkah. The incident is reported amid a sharp escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

. In Bangladesh, the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 today convicted and sentenced seven people, including Awami League (AL) General Secretary and former minister Obaidul Quader, to death in a case of crimes against humanity over killings during the July uprising in Dhaka.The three-member second tribunal, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, pronounced the judgement this afternoon. The other convicts in the case are- AFM Bahauddin Nasim, Mohammad Ali Arafat, Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, Md Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Md Saddam Hossain and Sheikh Wali Asif Inan.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. India’s retail inflation accelerated to 4.82 per cent in August on an annual basis, remaining above the Reserve Bank of India’s target of four per cent for the third consecutive month this year. The August inflation reading was higher than the 4.45 per cent recorded in July as food prices remained elevated.According to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, inflation in rural areas increased to 5.23 per cent, while in urban regions it rose to 4.31 per cent. The food inflation rate, based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index, stood at 5.95 per cent last month, up from 5.52 per cent in the preceding month.According to the data, the increase in inflation during the last month was mainly attributed to rising prices in personal care, social protection, restaurants and accommodation services, food, beverages and intoxicants. The top items showing high inflation at the all-India combined level included Silver, Gold, Diamond and Platinum Jewellery, Ginger, Onion and Garlic. In contrast, items with lowest inflation included Tomato, Potato, Car, Lady’s finger, Parwal and Kundru.

. In men’s cricket, India will begin their three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi this evening. The match will start at 7 PM Indian time. The remaining two matches of the series will be played at the same venue on Tuesday and Thursday.Shreyas Iyer will lead India, with Tilak Varma as his deputy. Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has also been named in the team.India have won eight of their nine T20Is against Afghanistan, with one match ending without a result.Meanwhile, Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory for spectators, as the match coincides with the second and final day of the BRICS Summit. Traffic restrictions, diversions and parking regulations will be in place in and around the stadium and parts of central Delhi from 2 PM onwards.Spectators have been advised to plan their journeys, use alternate routes and use only designated entry, parking and app-based taxi pick-up and drop-off points.

. In Hockey, India’s men’s and women’s teams have clinched the Junior Asia Cup titles at Moqi in China today. The Indian Men’s team defeated South Korea four-one in the final to successfully defend its title. Ajeet Yadav, Anmol Ekka, Prabhdeep Singh and Ashu Maurya scored for India. With this victory, India became the first team in the history of the tournament to win the Men’s title four times, following earlier triumphs in 2015, 2023 and 2024.The Indian women’s team also emerged victorious, defeating hosts China one-nil in the final. Sanika Chandrakant Mane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to secure the title for India. The victory completed a hat-trick of Junior Asia Cup titles for the Indian women’s team, which had previously won in 2023 and 2024.Both the Indian men’s and women’s teams have also qualified for the Junior Hockey World Cup by winning their respective Asia Cup titles.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated India’s Junior Women’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asia Cup title with an unbeaten campaign. In a social media post, Mr. Modi said the team’s success reflects the talent and determination of the players and extended his best wishes to the entire team.The Prime Minister also congratulated the Junior Men’s Hockey Team on winning the Asia Cup with an emphatic 4-1 victory over South Korea in the final. Describing the achievement as remarkable, Mr. Modi said it reflects the immense talent of the young players.Home Minister Amit Shah has congratulated junior women’s hockey team on winning the Asia Cup and bringing pride and joy to the entire nation. Sharing a social media post, Mr Shah said that their victory and dominant display of sporting prowess will inspire more budding players to join the list of India’s champions. Mr Shah also congratulated Indian junior men’s hockey team for winning the Asia Cup. He added that with the vigour and command of the game, they have once again demonstrated that true mettle of Indian sportsmanship and set an inspiring example for others to follow.
